text: Hãy đi xem code của dự án này. Đọc README.md rồi duyệt cấu trúc thư mục. Sau đó dùng spawn_agent giao việc cho nhiều agent con chạy song song, mỗi agent đọc kỹ một phần: (1) pipeline detect, mask và inpaint trong app/detector và app/inpaint, (2) các router API trong app/routers, (3) frontend app/static/js, (4) bộ test trong tests, (5) agent harness trong app/agent, (6) A.I mode và các nhà cung cấp AI. Dùng wait_agent lấy báo cáo của từng agent. Cuối cùng tổng hợp một bản đồ kiến trúc ngắn gọn và nêu 5 điểm đáng ngờ hoặc có thể là bug, kèm đường dẫn file và dòng.

1 # Manga & Webtoon Translator Studio 2 3 [![Release Gate](https://github.com/tuantran00541-spec/manga-translator/actions/workflows/release-gate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tuantran00541-spec/manga-translator/actions/workflows/release-gate.yml) 4 [![Python 3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/) 5 [![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/backend-FastAPI-009688?logo=fastapi&logoColor=white)](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) 6 [![CPU First](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-CPU--first-222222)](#cpu-first-design) 7 8 **Translate a manga, manhwa or webtoon chapter on your own computer, with no GPU.** 9 10 Give it a chapter URL or a folder of images. It erases the original lettering, translates it and letters the translation back, and leaves every step open to the editor: nothing becomes the final chapter until you say so. 11 12 **Import → Slice → Detect → Clean → Review → OCR → Translate → Letter → Render → Export** 13 14

15 16 17 18

19 20

RAW → CLEAN → translated to Vietnamese by A.I mode, cropped from page 3 of Pepper&Carrot episode 38, “The Healer” by David Revoy, CC BY 4.0. The lettering was erased and the translation lettered by this app.

21 22 > **Automation proposes. Editorial state decides. Published artifacts must match the current state.** 23 24 ## What it does well 25 26 ### It erases text without wrecking the art 27 28 Cleanup runs on a mask of the letters themselves, not on detector rectangles. A comic-text-detector mask head reads the letters; the app adds a thin outline round every letter, then grows into the glow and shadow round it. Art that touches the letters stays. 29 30 Two whole webtoon chapters on a 4-core GitHub runner, real models, 2 page workers (evidence on the `audit-evidence` branch): 31 32 | Chapter | Slices | Text blocks | Time | Text left | 33 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 34 | The World After the End, ch. 254 | 68 | 167 | 418 s | **0** | 35 | Youngest Scion of the Mages, ch. 137 | 52 | 145 | 332 s | **0** | 36 37 Times move with the runner's CPU: the first chapter took 418 s and 446 s on two different CPU models. 38 39 On labelled synthetic text, the mask erases 73.7 % of what has to go at 73.1 % precision; the hand-tuned rules it replaced managed 65.4 % at 43.1 %. 40 41 ### The same image always gives the same result 42 43 A page cleaned twice gives the same pixels, on any CPU: the sampled slices of a whole chapter came out pixel-identical on two different CPU models. The one source of run-to-run drift, a random seed in the background-colour clustering, is fixed. 44 45 ### It is fast where it matters 46 47 - A 2.4 M-parameter detector finds the text of a slice in a few packed passes (halves side by side, near-native bands, page-scale columns for big captions), on the OpenVINO runtime when available. 48 - The letter-mask model runs about 40× faster than the released one with identical masks. 49 - LaMa fills each region in one downscaled pass (512 px long side), and only where a fill is needed: a hole ringed by one colour, of any shade, is filled flat with no model run. 50 51 ### The whole chapter runs on a laptop 52 53 Everything on the cleanup path is a small ONNX model on the CPU. Nothing needs a GPU or a cloud account; OCR and AI translation are optional layers around that. 54 55 ## Two ways to work 56 57 **By hand.** Import a chapter and clean it, then correct, OCR, translate and letter it in the browser workbench. Every step can be redone. 58 59 **A.I mode.** Paste a chapter URL with an AI key (or use Manga Cloud) and pick the target language: Vietnamese, English, Indonesian, Spanish, Portuguese, French or German. Four checkpoints run the chapter, and the lettered result opens in the same editor: 60 61 1. **Scan** the raw slices: skip credit and textless slices, keep series logos untouched. 62 2. **Clean** the text (Kiuyha + LaMa). Meanwhile the chapter's names and terms are read into a glossary. 63 3. **Review** each raw and clean slice pair: erase missed text, repaint leftovers, restore art erased by mistake. 64 4. **Translate** each slice from its raw image with the glossary, naming each text's role and container; the font follows them, so one kind of text always looks the same. 65 66 An optional **Jev** pass grades every translated line and rewrites the weak ones. 67 68 Across five chapters of five series, A.I mode cost about **$0.07** of model calls per chapter. 69 70 ## The workflow 71 72 | Stage | What happens | 73 | --- | --- | 74 | **1. Import** | Images, ZIP/CBZ archives, or chapter URLs | 75 | **2. Slice** | Long webtoon pages become processing-friendly slices | 76 | **3. Detect** | Text blocks and a letter mask for each (letters, outlines, glow) | 77 | **4. Clean** | LaMa inpainting on letter masks, leftover passes, manual repair | 78 | **5. Review** | Unified canvas workspace and editorial corrections | 79 | **6. OCR** | MangaOCR + PP-OCRv6 hybrid recognition | 80 | **7. Translate** | Batch text translation or two-image vision translation | 81 | **8. Letter** | Text objects, geometry, typography, fonts by text role | 82 | **9. Render** | Revision-safe page publication | 83 | **10. Export** | Stitched chapter ZIP | 84 85 ## Features 86 87 ### Import and slicing 88 89 - PNG, JPEG, WEBP and BMP; ZIP and CBZ chapters 90 - The browser extension: open the chapter in your own Chrome or Edge, click once, and its images go into the app. Sites behind Cloudflare that block Playwright work, because your browser has already loaded the pages. 91 - Chapter URLs through HTTP and Playwright: relative URLs, srcset, lazy-load attributes and scroll-based discovery, with site adapters where a fast path is stable 92 - Bounded downloads and upload validation 93 - Long pages are cut in low-content bands, never at a fixed height. Source-page identity and stitch ownership are recorded, so the chapter is rebuilt with no duplicated or missing pixels. 94 95 ### Detection 96 97 The Kiuyha ONNX text detector (`models/kiuyha_text_1280.onnx`) finds the text blocks of a slice. Each block gets an erase mask: 98 99 - letters read by the mask head of comic-text-detector (`models/ctd_seg.onnx`), at full and half size 100 - a thin outline round every letter, even one the same colour as the background 101 - glow and shadow: smooth pixels unlike the colours round the block, grown out from the letters 102 - art touching the letters stays: growth that runs off the block is dropped 103 - a box holding two separate captions becomes two texts 104 - text across a slice seam is detected once on a strip over the cut and joins the block it belongs to 105 106 Detection records keep their source model and review state. [docs/detection.md](docs/detection.md) explains how and why. 107 108 ### Artwork-safe cleanup 109 110 - LaMa inpainting with a zeroed hole, and nearby text not erased yet hidden from its context 111 - leftover passes only where the letter model still reads text after cleanup 112 - flat fill instead of LaMa where a hole is ringed by one colour 113 - dynamic and fixed LaMa backends, with tiling for the fixed 512 model 114 - manual repaint, mask reset, and preserve/skip regions 115 - a restore brush that puts the original page back where the cleanup went too far; the page keeps it through later repaints 116 117 Uncertain detections, watermarks and review-only regions are not silently promoted to destructive cleanup. 118 119 ### OCR 120 121 - **PP-OCRv6 / PaddleOCR** for Japanese, Chinese, Korean and English. On 110 Black Jack text boxes it missed 3.2% of the dialogue characters, against 13% for MangaOCR, which the app used before. 122 123 OCR is chapter-aware and revision-safe, and keeps the source lettering's colour, position and size as hints for typesetting. 124 125 ### Translation 126 127 **Text translation.** Batch existing text objects through configured OpenAI-compatible providers, with stable IDs, stale-write protection and budget controls where pricing is known. 128 129 **Vision translation.** Send the **ORIGINAL** and **CLEAN** versions of a slice together with the existing text-object IDs and their regions. The model translates only objects that already exist; geometry, placement, colour and size stay editor-owned. 130 131 ### Lettering and fonts 132 133 The browser workbench edits translated text, font, size, weight, stroke, background, alignment, region geometry and manual text objects in one Review workspace. 134 135 - **Undo and redo** (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) for text edits, moves, resizes, styles, new and deleted text objects, and whole find-and-replace or preset runs. 136 - **Keyboard proofreading**: A/D move between slices, Alt+Up/Down between text objects, Enter edits the translation, Ctrl+Enter saves and goes to the next one, Esc returns to the page; `?` lists every shortcut. 137 - **Proofreading panel** (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H): every source line and translatio … [13811 characters cut] … sts its limits and admin commands. 291 292 | Area | Variables | 293 | --- | --- | 294 | A.I upstream | `GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_BASE`, `GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_KEY`, `GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_MODEL`, `GATEWAY_PRICE_INPUT_PER_M`, `GATEWAY_PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_M`; for Azure OpenAI also `GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_AUTH=api-key` and `GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_MAX_TOKENS_FIELD=max_completion_tokens` | 295 | Login email | `GATEWAY_RESEND_API_KEY`, `GATEWAY_MAIL_FROM`, `GATEWAY_DEV_LOGIN=1` (shows the code instead of mailing it, local testing only) | 296 | Wallet | `GATEWAY_FEE_PERCENT` (5), `GATEWAY_CHAPTER_ESTIMATE_USD` (0.30), `GATEWAY_VND_PER_USD` (26000), `GATEWAY_TOPUPS_VND`, `GATEWAY_TOPUPS_USD` | 297 | payOS (VietQR) | `GATEWAY_PAYOS_CLIENT_ID`, `GATEWAY_PAYOS_API_KEY`, `GATEWAY_PAYOS_CHECKSUM_KEY`, `GATEWAY_PAYOS_FEE_PERCENT` (0); webhook `/v1/billing/payos/webhook` | 298 | Lemon Squeezy (cards) | `GATEWAY_LS_API_KEY`, `GATEWAY_LS_STORE_ID`, `GATEWAY_LS_VARIANT`, `GATEWAY_LS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `GATEWAY_LS_FEE_PERCENT` (5), `GATEWAY_LS_FEE_FIXED_USD` (0.50); webhook `/v1/billing/lemonsqueezy/webhook` | 299 | Other | `GATEWAY_DB`, `GATEWAY_ADMIN_KEY`, `GATEWAY_RETURN_URL`, `GATEWAY_HOST`, `GATEWAY_PORT`, `GATEWAY_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | 300 301 Signed-in users see their balance and every top-up and chapter charge, and can sign out on every device or delete their account from the A.I mode panel. A payOS top-up is credited once, when its webhook reports the exact amount. A Lemon Squeezy top-up is a one-time order at a custom price on one product variant; a refund takes the credit back. 302 303 ## Runtime settings 304 305 Detection, inpainting, OCR and rendering thresholds are fixed constants in `app/parameters.py`. Only operational settings read environment variables: 306 307 | Area | Variables | 308 | --- | --- | 309 | Processing | `MANGA_PIPELINE_DEFAULT_WORKERS`, `MANGA_PIPELINE_SLICE_WORKER_LIMIT`, `MANGA_USE_DYNAMIC_LAMA`, `MANGA_INPAINT_PRELOAD`, `MANGA_FIXED_LAMA_*` | 310 | ONNX Runtime | `MANGA_ORT_PROVIDER`, `MANGA_ORT_REQUIRE_PROVIDER`, `MANGA_ORT_INTRA_OP_THREADS`, `MANGA_ORT_OPENVINO_*`, `MANGA_ORT_CPU_MEM_ARENA`, `MANGA_ORT_MEM_PATTERN`, `MANGA_ORT_SERIALIZE_INFERENCE` | 311 | OCR | `MANGA_PPOCRV6_TIER`, `MANGA_PPOCRV6_TEXTLINE_ORIENTATION`, `MANGA_OCR_TARGET_SELECTION`, `MANGA_OCR_IMAGE_CACHE_MB`, `MANGA_OCR_JOB_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT`, `MANGA_OCR_JOB_ACTIVE_LIMIT` | 312 | Agent | `MANGA_AGENT_MODE=0` turns the Agent screen's routes off | 313 | Access | `MANGA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`: extra host names the app answers to, comma separated (loopback always works; add the machine's LAN name or IP to open it from another device) | 314 | Network and AI | `MANGA_DOWNLOAD_WORKERS`, `MANGA_DOWNLOAD_JS_NAVIGATION_TIMEOUT_MS`, `MANGA_REMOTE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `MANGA_TRANSLATION_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `MANGA_TRANSLATION_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | 315 316 ## CPU-first design 317 318 The supported baseline is CPU execution, tuned for bounded desktop-class workloads instead of a GPU: 319 320 - two page workers by default, small enough that heavy inference kernels do not fight for the same memory bandwidth 321 - conservative ONNX Runtime threading 322 - OpenVINO for the text detector on x86-64 Windows and Linux; standard ONNX Runtime elsewhere and for the letter mask and LaMa, whose input sizes vary 323 - decoded-page caching for repeated OCR work 324 - bounded downloads with transient retries 325 - short manifest lock windows 326 327 ## Safety by design 328 329 Safety is part of the processing model, not only of deployment. The app protects: 330 331 - remote URL imports against SSRF and unsafe address ranges 332 - managed files against path escape 333 - uploads and archives against oversized payloads 334 - decoded images against excessive pixel counts 335 - browser requests against unsafe remote targets 336 - custom AI endpoints against invalid or untrusted URLs 337 - rendered and exported artifacts against stale editor state 338 339 A deployment that faces the network still needs normal firewall and authentication controls. 340 341 ## Architecture 342 343 ~~~text 344 Browser Workbench 345 │ 346 FastAPI 347 │ 348 ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐ 349 │ │ │ 350 ▼ ▼ ▼ 351 Processing Editorial AI 352 Pipeline State Providers 353 │ │ │ 354 Detect · OCR · Text · Geometry Translate · QC 355 Inpaint · Render · Typography 356 └─────────────────┼─────────────────┘ 357 ▼ 358 Revision-safe artifacts 359 │ 360 ▼ 361 Stitched ZIP export 362 ~~~ 363 364 For implementation details see [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). 365 366 ## Documentation 367 368 - [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) 369 - [Text detection](docs/detection.md) 370 - [Comic font library](docs/comic-fonts.md) 371 - [Deploying the gateway](docs/DEPLOY.md) 372 - [UI guidelines](docs/UI_GUIDELINES.md) 373 - [Security history](docs/SECURITY_HISTORY.md) 374 375 ## Development 376 377 ~~~bash 378 python -m pip install -r requirements-test.txt 379 make test # regression tests 380 make test-browser # browser and runtime checks 381 make health 382 make release-check # the full release gate 383 make docker-up 384 ~~~ 385 386 The release path covers source compilation, regression tests, browser and runtime checks, OCR and provider contracts, mask authority, geometry and revision safety, long-image behaviour, and the connected product flow: **processed page → OCR/text object → translation → render → chapter ZIP**. Production ONNX binaries are not in Git, so model-dependent checks run separately. 387 388 To clean a whole real chapter with the real models and see the speed and the text left behind, run the **Chapter run** workflow from the Actions tab. To run A.I mode on a chapter and get every page image and its cost, run **A.I cost**. Both save their results to the `audit-evidence` branch, with a side-by-side image per text block. 389 390 ## Project layout 391 392 ~~~text 393 app/ 394 detector/ text detection (Kiuyha) and letter masks 395 downloader/ HTTP, Playwright, adapters and slicing 396 inpaint/ LaMa, flat fill and mask geometry safety 397 ocr/ MangaOCR + PP-OCRv6 398 translation/ text and two-image vision translation 399 ai_mode/ the A.I checkpoints, glossary and Jev pass 400 render/ typography, font catalog and lettering fonts 401 visual_qc/ Gemini and DeepSeek image helpers used by A.I mode 402 routers/ FastAPI API surface 403 static/ browser workbench 404 pipeline*.py chapter processing and runtime coordination 405 gateway/ Manga Cloud: accounts, wallet, metered A.I upstream 406 tests/ correctness and release regressions 407 models/ local model artifacts 408 data/ runtime chapter data 409 docs/ engineering documentation 410 scripts/ release, browser and benchmark tooling 411 ~~~ 412 413 ## Current limitations 414 415 The project speeds up chapter production; it does not replace professional redraw and lettering. 416 417 - **Stylised sound effects are mostly left as art**: the letter model reads story lettering, not drawn SFX, and Korean SFX and props text can stay in a machine-only run. 418 - **A glowing title can leave a faint smear** where the glow was erased. 419 - **Text painted into the art** (signs, screens) may be translated as plain text and lettered over it. 420 - **Vietnamese compound words** can split across two lines. 421 - **Watermarks and site banners** are only partly erased. 422 - On large manga pages with heavy black art, the cleanup can take a stroke of art that the detector boxed as text; the restore brush puts it back. 423 - **Western comic pages are not the target**: the tool is tuned for webtoons. Small balloons that hug their text can be erased whole, and the text of balloons standing close together is joined into one block, so its translation runs over the art. 424 - Perspective or warped lettering, curved text, hand-drawn SFX recreation, ambiguous OCR, heavily protected reader sites and typography that needs artistic judgment still need a person. 425 426 The strongest use is a **reviewable production workstation with automation**, not a black-box batch converter. 427 428 ## Philosophy 429 430 Detection, cleanup, OCR, translation, typography and AI help are all allowed to make mistakes. The editor can inspect, correct, reject, repaint, resize, retranslate or restyle any of them before anything becomes the published chapter. 431 432 > **The page belongs to the editor.** 433 434 ## License 435 436 Copyright (C) 2026 tuantran00541-spec. The code is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](LICENSE): you may use, change and share it, and anyone who runs a changed version as a network service must offer its source to that service's users. 437 438 Bundled third-party parts keep their own licenses: 439 440 - **Fonts:** SIL Open Font License, see `app/static/fonts/licenses/`. 441 - **Vietnamese word list:** MIT, see `app/render/vi_words.LICENSE.txt`. 442 - **Models:** downloaded at install time, under their own authors' terms.
